newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Low foreign interest hike Russian T-bill yields.
newsitem.headline: Low foreign interest hike Russian T-bill yields.

text.p: Prices of Russian domestic government securities rose at auction on Wednesday when foreigners worried by U.S. interest rate policy sat out, dealers said.
They forecast a rise in prices of short-term paper on Thursday as investors moved from longer paper which now have similar yields to the lesser-risk short-term issues.

The Finance Ministry auctioned a 364-day T-bill (series 21078) at an average yield of 20.00 percent and an additional 704-day tranche of OFZ bond (series 25001) at an average price of 102.06 percent and yield of 18.56 percent.
The average yield in secondary trade on Tuesday was 19.29.
"The premium was possible thanks to non-residents, who are waiting for the decision on U.S. rates," said ABN-Amro dealer Andrei Babenko.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee is to convey a decision on whether to change its rates today.
Babenko said the second auction of 364-day paper saw higher prices after low demand at the first.
"That is why people bid for a premium at the second auction," he said.

ING-Bank trader Maxim Safonov forecast a price rise in shorter paper on Thursday, saying investors saw shorter issues as more profitable since yields on long-term paper were about the same as on lower-risk short-term paper,

"The resistance level will be at 19 percent due to the central bank's recent regular statements," he said. "No one will go fight it and the rates could stay flat for quite a long time with one percent fluctuations."
Central bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Wednesday the bank had no intention of pressing government paper yields down any further.
